data.exact_reserve_text: Reserves established in 2017 and 2018 in respect of the Atlantic basin hurricanes, Californian wildfires and Japanese typhoons have, in aggregate, proved to be broadly adequate. Adverse development on Hurricane Michael and Typhoon Jebi has been offset by favourable development elsewhere. Much of the adverse development has been absorbed into the retrocession in place; some of the reductions have delivered a net benefit.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 435 shows an opening gross claims outstanding of GBP 1,215.8m and experienced net favourable prior-year development of approximately GBP 56.8m (gross release), representing ~4.7% of opening reserves. The release reflects favourable development across older underwriting years which more than offset adverse movements arising from prior events such as Hurricane Michael and Typhoon Jebi; much adverse development was absorbed by retrocession. In 2019 the syndicate incurred catastrophe losses from Hurricane Dorian and Typhoons Faxai and Hagibis, which the report states were within modelled expectations. US casualty lines saw reserve strengthening due to poor performance in General Liability and Medical Malpractice, partly offset by favourable Workers' Compensation experience.
raw_causal_phrases: Reserves established in 2017 and 2018 in respect of the Atlantic basin hurricanes, Californian wildfires and Japanese typhoons have, in aggregate, proved to be broadly adequate.
Adverse development on Hurricane Michael and Typhoon Jebi has been offset by favourable development elsewhere.
Much of the adverse development has been absorbed into the retrocession in place; some of the reductions have delivered a net benefit.

The 2019 result was impacted by several significant catastrophe events. Of particular note in the year were Hurricane Dorian and Typhoons Faxai and Hagibis. Losses from these events were within modelled expectations.

US Casualty business has experienced some poor performance in 2019 particularly in General Liability and to a lesser extent the Medical Malpractice portfolios. We have materially strengthened the reserves in those areas

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (gross) was calculated from the published gross claims development table (claims triangle) on page 34 by comparing current estimates to the previous diagonal for underwriting years up to 2017. A reinsurance-to-close (Syndicate 2255) transaction occurred at 1 January 2018 (note 20) which may distort comparability of some development measures; the report contains narrative references to net movements but gross quantification was taken from the triangle. Some LOB-specific reserve movements are described qualitatively only (e.g. 'materially strengthened the reserves' for US Casualty) and no gross amounts by LOB were provided.
